title: manuscript-guard setup answers
description: design/setup.yaml: what the authors chose when the project was set up, each answer at the place `manuscript-guard setup questions` names for its question. `setup apply` writes the project from it, each setting only where it is blank, and records the date it did. paper.yaml and authors.yaml hold the settings and are what every check reads; nothing is checked against this file. A value of `later` puts a decision off: nothing is written for it, and `manuscript-guard next` asks it when it is due.

applied_on.description: Written by `setup apply`: the day it wrote the project from these answers.

start.description: How the manuscript is written: `markdown`, `latex`, or the name of a .docx in the folder, brought in from Word.

title.description: The working title. Empty with a Word paper: the title its Title style holds.

language.description: British or American English, or another language, for which no English is declared and the writing checks, which read English, do not apply.

study_type.description: One of the designs paper.yaml's study_type takes: `setup questions` lists them, and an answer outside them keeps its question open.

reporting_guideline.description: The guidelines the paper follows; empty for none yet.

journal.description: `later`, `help` (the journal is chosen with the journal-profile skill), the name of a profile the project has, or the journal named, whose profile `setup apply` starts.

authors.description: Every author, in the order of the byline, each as they gave their name.

affiliations.description: Each affiliation's text, as printed: "Department, Institution, City, Country".

declarations.description: `given`: each author's funding, competing interests and CRediT roles are written in their entry above, as they gave them; `later`: none is asked now.

statistician.description: `later`, an author by family name, full name or ORCID iD, or someone who is not an author.

ethics_lead.description: `later`, `none` where the study needs no approval, or the author who holds it and the approval's reference.

analysis.description: The language of the analysis: `other` takes its outputs in with `harvest`.

folder.description: With `project`: the folder of the project the data are in.

publishable.description: With `project`: whether the data may be published with the repository.

minimum_cell_count.description: The smallest count the data's custodian lets be published; 1 where they set none.

registration.description: `none`, `later`, or each registration's identifier as the registry writes it.

git.description: Make the folder a git repository.

visibility.description: Where the repository is shared: on a public site, a private one, or nowhere.

sources_in_git.description: In a private repository: commit the stored copies of the cited works.

github_actions.description: Write the workflow that runs check on each push and pull request.

earlier_work.description: The authors have published on these data before: an abstract, a preprint or an article.
